subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration fit & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 15:00:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration fit & next steps

Alex — thanks for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

High-level pain points you called out:
- Freshness/latency on semantic search (current embedding infra is 200-300ms per query at peak).
- Cost per query for chat/assistant is higher than expected; priority to reduce per-token unit economics.
- Need structured, deterministic responses for customer-facing flows (billing, account status).
- Desire for streaming responses in the web UI to improve perceived latency.

Goals we agreed on:
- Reduce embedding query cost by ~30–40% and improve tail latency to <150ms for typical queries.
- Provide streaming, partial responses for chat while preserving structured outputs for downstream systems.
- Support embeddings + reranking pipeline for search with an easy SDK integration path.

Product fit / integration notes from today:
- SDK changes: we recommend using the Redwood SDK (JS/py) which supports streaming chunks and built-in function-calling helpers. The SDK will handle chunk re-assembly and event hooks for the UI.
- Function calling / structured outputs: function-call schemas can be used to produce typed JSON responses. This matches your need for deterministic billing/account responses. We can ship a sample schema for your billing endpoints.
- Streaming: streaming works with the hosted API and Dedicated. For Private (VPC/on-prem) we support streaming but it requires websocket ingress and a small proxy configuration — we can scope this in the SOW.
- Embeddings & reranking: recommended flow is to index dense embeddings in your vector DB, call Redwood to compute embeddings (or host embeddings locally with our private option), and use our lightweight reranker model to rescore top-k results. This reduces downstream compute and improves hit-rate.

Attachments: Redwood-Integration-Approach.pdf (high-level architecture + timeline), sdk-snippet.py (short example), demo-recording-20270415.mp4 (recording of today’s call).

Next steps / action items:
1) I’ll share a short technical doc + SDK snippet today (attached).
2) Schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive next week with Vivek and your infra team to go over streaming and Private deployment requirements.
3) We’ll draft a rough SOW and timeline (2–4 week PoC if we scope only embeddings + streaming).

Can you confirm:
- Priority order for the three goals above (embedding cost/latency, streaming UI, structured outputs)?
- Any compliance constraints we should factor into the SOW (SAML, IP allowlist, SOC2 evidence)?

Thanks,

—Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration fit & next steps

Marissa — great recap, thanks. Quick answers and a couple follow-ups: 

Priority (high -> low):
1) Structured outputs for billing/account flows (determinism is critical)
2) Embedding cost/latency (we need ~150ms p50 or better for our search UX)
3) Streaming (important for perceived speed but can be deferred if it increases infra complexity)

Follow-ups / questions:
- Security/compliance: we are SOC2 compliant and need to ensure evidence for data handling. Can you confirm what evidence Redwood provides for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private?
- Quantization / model performance: can you share guidance on model quantization compatibility (e.g., int8) and expected latency impact?
- Latency numbers: can you share 95th/99th percentile numbers for generation and embeddings on Dedicated (g4dn-like) and Hosted?

Yes to a technical deep-dive. Our infra lead (Taylor) will join; I’ll introduce them in the next thread. We’re targeting a PO decision within 3–4 weeks if the PoC looks good.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Johnson
Director of Product, Acme Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration fit & next steps

Alex — thanks, helpful priority ordering. Quick answers inline and a couple of attachments/snippets: 

Security/compliance:
- Hosted: we provide SOC 2 Type II report excerpts and a security package (data flow diagrams, encryption at rest/in transit, deletion policy).
- Dedicated: same artifacts plus network isolation docs and per-tenant logging options.
- Private: customer-managed control plane; we provide an integration checklist and on-prem deployment guide. I attached the redacted SOC2 excerpt in the PDF.

Quantization / model perf:
- Our runtime supports int8 quantization for many open models; typical latency improvements ~20–40% depending on model size and sequence length. We’ll validate on your model/sequence profiles in the PoC.

Latency (typical numbers, op-mode dependent):
- Hosted (n1-standard GPU): embeddings p50 ~30–50ms, p95 ~120ms; generation token latency p50 ~8–12ms/token.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pool): embeddings p50 ~20–35ms, p95 ~80–100ms; generation token latency p50 ~6–10ms/token.
- Note: exact numbers depend on batch size and KV cache reuse; we’ll run benchmarks with your payloads.

Streaming & structured outputs:
- Streaming is supported for both Hosted and Dedicated out of the box. For Private, we need a small websocket proxy; we can scope that in the SOW.
- Attached sdk-snippet.py shows function-calling + streaming handler (JS/py examples available).

Proposed PoC scope (2–4 weeks):
1) Integrate embeddings + reranker for a 10k test corpus and measure recall/latency.
2) Implement function-calling schema for 3 billing/account flows and verify deterministic output.
3) Optional: enable streaming in the UI prototype (depends on private vs hosted).

Next steps I’ll take this afternoon:
- Share a non-binding PoC SOW + timeline (attached draft).
- Propose 3 slots for technical deep-dive next week.

Action: Vivek — can you take the lead on the technical deep-dive? Specifically: streaming proxy requirements, quantization testing plan, and perf benchmark plan.

Alex — if that looks good I’ll loop Taylor in and we can book the call.

Best,
—Marissa
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
